A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same AlphaEdit research work. Their complete 32-page documents, including equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–D, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original knowledge-editing experiments, general-capability evaluations, sensitivity analyses and runtime measurements in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including the editing comparisons and supplementary experiments in Tables 1–7.

M1.justification: The null-space projection, editing objectives and final parameter update in Equations 9–14 are unchanged. New Appendix B.4 elaborates the existing solution without modifying the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Counterfact, ZsRE, the six general-capability tasks, KnowEdit subsets, LEME and MQuAKE. The appendix coverage was already present in v3.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains FT, MEND, InstructEdit, ROME, MEMIT, PRUNE and RECT; Table 2 retains SERAC, GRACE and MELO. Comparator membership also matches in the remaining tables and figures.

E3.justification: The 2,000-sample, batch-size-100 protocol in Section 4.2 is unchanged, as are model configurations, evaluation metrics, preprocessing and the additional testing procedures in Appendix C.

E4.justification: The case studies, reduced-batch capability tests, representation-shift analyses, semantic-category comparisons and sensitivity to the data used for estimating K0 are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: The tables retain their uncertainty reporting, including Table 4's standard-deviation description, and plotted uncertainty is unchanged. No run-count, seed or statistical-testing information is added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7, experimental plots and generated case-study outputs retain the same results. For example, Table 1 reports AlphaEdit's LLaMA3 Counterfact efficacy as 98.90±0.10 in both versions.

T1.justification: New Appendix B.4 adds intermediate differentiation and factorization steps using projector symmetry and idempotence to derive the existing update (Equations 31–34). The objective and final solution remain unchanged, and v3's invertibility argument is retained as B.5.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same knowledge-preservation and editing-improvement claims, including the reported 36.7% average improvement and single-line projection modification.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning overfitting and knowledge preservation are unchanged. The memory-based-method tradeoff in Appendix C.5 and the unexplored multimodal and reasoning-model extensions in Section 6 also remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The editing layers, optimization settings, projection cutoff, A40 hardware, covariance-estimation instructions, runtime documentation and code-access information are unchanged. Appendix B.4 adds algebraic explanation without new implementation settings.

R1.justification: Section 5, the cited works and the reference list are unchanged. The new derivation introduces no additional citations or revised positioning relative to prior research.

P1.justification: v4 adds a short derivation subsection, updates Section 3.3's cross-reference and renumbers the invertibility subsection. Author affiliations and corresponding-author markers also change; the remaining narrative is unchanged.

P2.justification: The added displayed equations tighten spacing on page 20 and move Appendix C's introduction to page 21, above the existing case study. Figures and tables retain their content and display structure.

improvement.justification: v3 states the normal equation and final update without the intermediate factorization; v4's Appendix B.4 supplies that step, making the algebra modestly easier to check. The benefit is limited: its 'left-multiplying' wording incorrectly describes right multiplication, while the existing invertibility argument and empirical support remain unchanged.
